newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds firm with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds firm with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose early Thursday, lifted by firmer U.S. Treasuries after the release of U.S. October trade figures.
"We are following the Treasuries market," said a trader at a foreign bank. "It's calm, I do not expect big news today."
The 30-year Treasury bond yield was last four basis points lower at 6.66 percent. The U.S. October trade deficit came in at a lower-than-expected $7.99 billion.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 122.10, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 3/8 to 85-3/8.
Analysts said President Carlos Menem's decision late Wednesday to sign three decrees to reform labor legislation was welcome news which should support the market in the medium term.
Menem signed the decrees after failing to reach agreeement with unions, to begin the process of freeing up the labor market which has become a key government policy goal.
This is positive for Argentina's market because "Menem is being decisive," in pushing for this, said Agustin Etchebarne, chief economist at consultants C&E Consultores.
